sharding_decomposition.limitation: no shard-constrained Oracle exists in Research Part 1 (argine.research.oracle defines a global Belady variant and a per-LAYER one, never a per-shard one); a true (A) Sharded-LRU-vs-Sharded-Oracle / (B) Sharded-Oracle-vs-Global-Oracle / (C) total decomposition (section 19) therefore cannot be built from already-validated Part 1 components. This decomposition instead uses Global-LRU as the shared pivot between the structural and policy-information gaps, which needs no new, unvalidated oracle.

policy_information_gap.interpretation: Global-LRU vs Oracle-Global-Belady: both global cache scope -- isolates the cost of imperfect (causal) prediction alone, decomposed away from sharding.

structural_sharding_gap.interpretation: Runtime-Sharded-LRU vs Global-LRU: both causal, both zero future knowledge -- isolates the cost of the runtime's sharded architecture alone, decomposed away from any prediction/retention advantage.

total_observed_upper_bound_gap.interpretation: Runtime-Sharded-LRU vs Oracle-Global-Belady: the full observed gap against the real runtime's own architecture; approximately structural + policy-information above (miss counts need not add exactly linearly across policies).
